title: CoNP-completeness of binary directed chip-firing reachability
seo_title: Binary directed chip-firing reachability | Alec Kriebel
seo_description: A preprint on coNP-completeness of legal reachability for strongly connected directed multigraphs with binary multiplicities and nonnegative chip configurations.
author: Alec Kriebel
status: Unrefereed preprint; extensively AI-assisted. Mathematical review for this catalogue is pending.
abstract_original_complete: Ordinary legal chip-firing reachability is coNP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions for finite loopless strongly connected directed multigraphs, with binary adjacency entries and nonnegative binary initial and target configurations. We give an explicit reduction from the complement of the halting problem of Farrell and Levine. A finite-state cutoff controls an exact simulation, a gate supplies a cleanup reserve, and a marker forces that gate to have fired in every target-reaching word. Together with the prior coNP-membership theorem of Hujter, Kiss and Tóthmérész, this answers the historical general-digraph hardness question in the stated model. We credit earlier period, recurrence and reserve-simulation arguments. Exact-result, gadget and method priority, independence of discovery, and present-day openness remain unknown after a bounded source audit. This extensively AI-assisted note is unrefereed.
plain_language: A chip-firing move sends chips along every outgoing arc from a vertex. This paper studies whether some sequence of legal moves can reach one specified final arrangement. Its claimed result classifies that question as coNP-complete when the graph is a strongly connected directed multigraph and its arc multiplicities and chip counts are written in binary. The proof connects indefinite legal play in a source instance to reaching an explicitly calculated target in a larger graph.
exact_result: The language of well-formed triples (G,x,y), where G is a finite nonempty loopless strongly connected directed multigraph of varying vertex count, all adjacency entries and both nonnegative configurations are binary encoded, and there exists a finite sequential legal firing word from x to y, is coNP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. The empty word and stopping at an unstable configuration are allowed; malformed inputs are rejected.
interesting_mechanism: A gate becomes available only after a long exact simulation, while a marker makes every target-reaching sequence pass through that gate. The target is computed directly from the input; the reduction need not first find a recurrent configuration or write the potentially exponential simulation.
limits: Parallel arcs, large degrees and large chip counts are used; no simple-graph, unary, bounded-degree or bounded-chip-count classification is claimed.
This is specified-target legal reachability, not halting, rotor-routing or a statement about all inputs on a fixed graph.
The target configurations are nonnegative; signed intermediate normalization does not establish coNP membership for every signed formulation.

Existing source hardness, membership, period and reserve-simulation arguments are explicitly credited. Exact-result, gadget and method priority, independent discovery and current worldwide openness remain unknown.
